dedupe_keys.name: ooni open observatory of network interference open measurements of internet censorship blocking and network performance

description: OONI publishes what it calls the world's largest open dataset on internet censorship: millions of measurements collected by volunteers running OONI Probe in more than 200 countries since 2012. The measurements test the blocking of websites and apps and measure network speed and performance, and OONI's research reports use them to document events such as throttling of social media during protests and IP-based blocking during football streaming. Coverage: global, from 2012, wherever volunteers run the probe. Format and access: OONI Explorer for browsing, the OONI API for analysis and documented batch access for bulk data, with a tutorial notebook; free. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0, read from OONI's data licence file. Caveats: coverage depends on where and when volunteers test; OONI itself works on filtering bad measurements; the non-commercial licence limits reuse. Simulation uses: records of intentional network interference and service disruption by country and date support studies of telecom service resilience and of deliberate attacks on connectivity. Related records: IODA (data-ioda-internet-outage-detection) detects outages from other signals, and Cloudflare Radar (data-cloudflare-radar) reports traffic disruptions.
